subject: en
stem: What was the author commissioned to do about English public libraries?

options.B: Make a plan for their expansions

passage:
Ask people about public libraries and a certain image springs to mind: dusty, old-fashioned, the sort of place you enjoyed as a child but, rather like a British seaside town, would you go there now? And anyway-aren’t they all closing?

The reality is startlingly different, as I discovered when the culture department commissioned me to conduct an independent review of English public libraries, published yesterday. As I visited libraries up and down the country, I was surprised to learn there are more than twice the number of libraries (2,892) as there are branches of McDonald’s.

Enter any one of them and you will find a hive of activity, while books are, and should always be, at the heart of any library, a multitude of other services are offered: employment advice, language classes or digital access and support.

There are libraries with business and intellectual property centres, which can help business owners and entrepreneurs. Many have nurses on site to carry out basic health checks, with a link to the GP’s surgery, there are libraries where young people can borrow a Fifa-standard football free.

In return for all of this, you’ll be asked for precisely nothing. There will be no charge and you will never be asked to justify or explain yourself, you will simply be welcomed in, offered help if you need it, and left alone if you do not. There is no other institution, public or private, that can say the same. Yet still our libraries are often overlooked and underappreciated. There is an overall decline in visits and many are struggling as local authorities come under continued financial pressure.

The number of libraries that have closed since 2010 is disputed. An annual survey by the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy puts it at nearly 800 across the UK; official statistics held by the Arts Council record 230 in England. It is, of course, 230 libraries too many. So if we are to protect our libraries for future generations, we must raise awareness of them and the work they do.

The review recommends a national branding campaign to give libraries a stronger physical presence, the reintroduction of a scheme to enable members to use their card in any library in the country, and automatic memberships for children. If we don’t use them, we will end up losing them. And for those who haven’t been to a library for some time, they may be surprised by what they find.
explanation: 细节题。根据题干关键词 commissioned 回文定位第一段第二句：「as I discovered when the culture department commissioned me to conduct an independent review of English public libraries」（文化部委托我对英国公共图书馆开展独立调研）。D 项 Look into their current situation（调研其现状）与 conduct an independent review 是同义改写：look into = review（调查）。A 项「记录宝贵传统」、B 项「制定扩建计划」、C 项「获取读者意见」文中均未提及。故选 D。

stem: According to Paragraph 1, workers’ engagement with AI can ________.
passage:
According to our research, around one in five workers in the UK talk to AI like a friend, looking for guidance on personal and professional problems. Our data shows that engaging with AI like this can leave us feeling heard and less isolated. But, with this newfound connection, many of us share sensitive, sometimes highly confidential informational, even though over a third of people don’t realise that AI platforms may not be very good at keeping our secrets… secrets.

For business, the implications are worrying. Consider Microsoft Copilot, for example. It gains Microsoft broad rights to the data inputted or outputted by any user – rights to use this data in any way it sees fit; it can even share it with third parties. This means that any way it sees fit, it can even share it with third parties. This means that any sensitive business information could potentially be exposed to the world. Employers are taking note and taking action. According to our research, 25% have decided to either outright ban AI or regulate its use within their organisations. But even with these policies in place, some employees choose to break the rules. They have their reasons – around 63% of them report that using AI increases their productivity, and some even feel AI offers more help than their human colleagues.

The situation presents a delicate balance between leveraging AI for its productivity gains and risking confidential data exposure. Employers need to manage AI tools with the same level of care as any other form of data sharing or storage. There's also a knowledge gap that needs to be addressed — 40% of individuals surveyed are unsure about who retains ownership over the content produced by AI. By instilling best practices in AI engagement and creating policies that evolve with the technology, business can positively shift the AI landscape.

With AI's potential to simplify our professional lives, do the admin and enhance the work experience. It's up to us to navigate its usage cautiously so it supports us without compromising our privacy. There's no need to back away from progress, as long as we're equipped with the knowledge and tools to make sure AI remains a friend. And this is where the challenge lies. There are so many products out there, being promoted with huge advertising and marketing budgets, that it's easy to fall victim. But by building a culture of digital responsibility within our business, we can create a future where AI can help us without spilling the beans.
explanation: 细节题。根据题干提示定位第一段：「Our data shows that engaging with AI like this can leave us feeling heard and less isolated.」（像朋友一样与 AI 交流能让人感到被倾听、不那么孤立。）即 AI 能给人情感上的支持。B 项 give them emotional support 是 feeling heard and less isolated 的同义概括。A 项「促进职业进步」、C 项「维持动力」、D 项「改善职场沟通」均非第一段内容。故选 B。

stem: According to the first two paragraphs, the high-speed rail network in Italy________.

options.A: is seen by tourists as outdated
options.B: is a popular option for travelling
options.D: is an example of good maintenance

passage:
Since the 2008 launch of the high-speed rail network between Rome and Milan, trains have become the preferred means of travel across Italy for locals and tourists alike. Fast trains can cover the 500km between the two cities in three hours. The network also connects Naples, Bologna, Florence and Turin. In many cases, it is the best option— in terms of travel time and cost— for both leisure and business travellers.

This is why the recent severe delays caused by numerous maintenance works have thrown the rail industry into chaos at a time when most people head on holiday, which matters for business in a country where tourism accounts for 10 percent of GDP.

Disruptions have become increasingly frequent with train delays now a fixture in Italian media coverage. Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane, the publicly controlled group that owns train operator Trenitalia and the national train network RFI, said 23 percent of all high-speed trains it operated were late in 2023.

The huge improvements in Italy's obsolete infrastructure partly explained the disruption, said Ferrovie. RFI, the network operator, is the single largest European recovery fund beneficiary with planned investments of €24bn by 2026. Ferrovie will invest a total of €124bn in infrastructure over the next 10 years.

But lack of capacity is another problem. Transport economist Andrea Giuricin said the planned investments would bring improvements but disruptions in the meantime were inevitable. “We have a mixed system, there is no spare capacity and as soon as there’s a hiccup on the line, the situation becomes highly complex,” he said. A mixed system means that high-speed trains must travel on the regular tracks on certain routes or when passing through large cities. If there’s congestion or, for example, a local train breaks down, the entire high-speed network is affected.

One of the most important changes the upgrades will bring is the segregation of the high-speed line from the regular one in certain urban centres through the construction of underground rail links.

Improvements will also come from the high-density technology and satellite signalling that RFI has been investing in for years, say experts. It will allow for a reduction of the distance between high-speed trains travelling on the same line at any given time, which should mean a significant increase in capacity and traffic fluidity, according to Giuricin.
explanation: 细节题。根据题干提示定位前两段：「trains have become the preferred means of travel across Italy for locals and tourists alike... In many cases, it is the best option — in terms of travel time and cost — for both leisure and business travellers.」（高铁是当地人 and 游客 alike 的首选出行方式，在时间和费用上都是最佳选择。）B 项 is a popular option for travelling（是受欢迎的出行选择）准确概括。A 项「过时」与 preferred 矛盾，C 项「未被当地人充分利用」与文意相反，D 项「维护良好」与后文 delays 不符。故选 B。

options.D: enhancing the safety of high-speed trains

passage:
Since the 2008 launch of the high-speed rail network between Rome and Milan, trains have become the preferred means of travel across Italy for locals and tourists alike. Fast trains can cover the 500km between the two cities in three hours. The network also connects Naples, Bologna, Florence and Turin. In many cases, it is the best option— in terms of travel time and cost— for both leisure and business travellers.

This is why the recent severe delays caused by numerous maintenance works have thrown the rail industry into chaos at a time when most people head on holiday, which matters for business in a country where tourism accounts for 10 percent of GDP.

Disruptions have become increasingly frequent with train delays now a fixture in Italian media coverage. Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane, the publicly controlled group that owns train operator Trenitalia and the national train network RFI, said 23 percent of all high-speed trains it operated were late in 2023.

The huge improvements in Italy's obsolete infrastructure partly explained the disruption, said Ferrovie. RFI, the network operator, is the single largest European recovery fund beneficiary with planned investments of €24bn by 2026. Ferrovie will invest a total of €124bn in infrastructure over the next 10 years.

But lack of capacity is another problem. Transport economist Andrea Giuricin said the planned investments would bring improvements but disruptions in the meantime were inevitable. “We have a mixed system, there is no spare capacity and as soon as there’s a hiccup on the line, the situation becomes highly complex,” he said. A mixed system means that high-speed trains must travel on the regular tracks on certain routes or when passing through large cities. If there’s congestion or, for example, a local train breaks down, the entire high-speed network is affected.

stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 1 that the Silver Room Block Party________.

options.A: has been replaced by other festivals

passage:
In 2023, Chicago lost one of its most beloved street festivals. The Silver Room Block Party, staged by Hyde Park community leader Eric Williams, announced it would not return in 2024. What began as a small neighborhood gathering blossomed into a massive cultural event welcoming tens of thousands of people each year over nearly two decades before abruptly shutting down.

Williams pointed to rising production costs and declining attendee donations as primary reasons the Silver Room Block Party could not continue, highlighting a reality that all street festival organizers face right now. The cost of producing a street festival in Chicago has skyrocketed.

Security, entertainment, portable restrooms, insurance and even basics such as fencing and staffing have all become significantly more expensive. At the same time, donations at festival gates have dropped dramatically.

Chicago’s summer festivals are about more than just entertainment; they are economic engines that directly benefit the neighborhoods they’re in and the city of Chicago as whole. Street festivals drive foot traffic to local businesses and foster the kind of cultural vibrancy that makes our city special. We often hear people ask why we solicit donations at our entry points, especially when the city’s largest festivals like the Chicago Jazz Festival do not request donations. The fact is, unlike those large, city-produced music festivals, your neighborhood street festivals receive no city funding and rely on a combination of sponsorships, vendor fees and gate donations to cover their costs.

Wicker Park Fest has long been one of Chicago’s most anticipated summer festivals, drawing upward of 70,000 attendees for a full weekend of live indie music, local art, small business vendors and, most importantly, community connection. In 2024, Wicker Park Fest saw record-breaking attendance. Despite the turnout, gate donations reached their lowest point in our history. This year, we’ve been forced to scale back the footprint of the fest. We are eliminating a stage, booking fewer performers and making additional cuts to reduce our costs, all while striving to keep the festival as vibrant as ever, as supportive of local artists and businesses, and as true to Wicker Park’s unique spirit and reputation as festgoers have come to expect.

This summer, as you enjoy your favorite neighborhood street festival, I hope you’ll remember that they exist because of community support. A thriving summer festival season doesn’t happen by accident; It happens when we all chip in.

subject: en
stem: According to Paragraph 1, the practice of tipping in the U.S.

options.A: was regarded as a sign of generosity

passage:
U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than minimum wage. In the early 2010s, a wide range of businesses started processing purchases with iPads and other digital payment systems. These systems often prompted customers to tip for services that were not previously tipped

Today's tip requests are not often connected to the salary and service norms that used to determine when and how people tip. Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered. That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it.

It's becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand. And now tipping technology may even automatically add tips.

The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip. That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services. Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options often well above 20% of what they owe. The amounts have risen from 10% or less in the 1950s to 15% around the year 2000 to 20% or higher today. This increase is sometimes called tipflation — the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts

Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped services like in restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as U.S. $2.13 an hour. Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers

Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as cooks and dishwashers, to ensure that all employees were paid fair wages. Some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement toward no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.

So to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation. However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high a tip too often. And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous, and often completely disassociated from quality.
explanation: 细节题。根据题干 Paragraph 1 定位第一段：“U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips”（美国顾客历来会给那些大部分收入来自小费的人小费），可见小费是对服务的一种“奖赏”，与第二段“reward high-quality service”呼应，故选 C。A、B 未提及；D 与史实矛盾。

When it was established, the National Health Service (NHS) was visionary: offering high- quality, timely care to meet the dominant needs of the population it served. Nearly 75 years on, with the UK facing very different health challenges, it is clear that the model is out of date.

From life expectancy to cancer and infant mortality rates, we are lagging behind many of our peers. With more than 6.8 million on waitlists, healthcare is becoming increasingly inaccessible for those who cannot opt to pay for private treatment, and the cost of providing healthcare is increasingly squeezing our investment in other public services, As demand for health care continues to grow, pressures on the workforce-which is already near breaking point-will only become more acute.

Many of the answers to the crisis in health and care are well rehearsed, We need to be much better at reducing and diverting demand on health services, rather than simply managing it. Much more needs to be invested in communities and primary care to reduce our reliance on hospitals. And capacity in social care needs to be greater, to support the growing number of people living with long-term conditions.

Yet despite two decades of strategies and a number of major health reforms, we have failed to make meaningful progress on any of these aims, That is why the Reform think tank is launching a new programme of work entitled “Reimagining Health”, supported by ten former health ministers Together, we are calling for a much more open and honest conversation about the future of health in the UK, and an “urgent rethink" of the hospital-centric model we retain.

This must begin with the question of how we maximize the health of the nation, rather than “fx” the NHS. It is estimated, for example, that healthcare accounts for only about 20% of health outcomes. Much more important are the places we live, work and socialize-yet there is no clear cross-government strategy for improving these social determinants of health. passage:
Heat action plans, or HAPs, have been proliferating in India in the past few years. In general. an HAP spells out when and how officials should issue heat warnings and alert hospitals and other institutions. Nagpur's plan, for instance, calls for hospitals to set aside “cold wards” in the summer for treating heatstroke patients, and advises builders to give construction laborers a break from work on very hot days.

But implementation of existing HAPs has been uneven, according to a report from the Centre for Policy Research, a prominent Indian think tank. It reviewed 37 plans adopted by cities, states, or administrative districts. Many lack adequate finding, it found. And their triggering thresholds often are not customized to the local climate, says Dileep Lvalankar, director of the Indian Institute of Public Health, who has been closely inyolved in Ahmedabad's HAP, In some areas. high daytime temperatures alone might serve as an adequate trigger for alerts. But in other places, nighttime temperatures or humidity might be as important a gauge of risk as daytime highs

Mumbai's April heat stroke deaths highlighted the need for more nuanced and localized warnings, researchers say. That day's high temperature of roughly 36°C was 1'C shy of the heat wave alert threshold for coastal cities set by national meteorological authorities, But the effects of the heat were amplified by humidity-an often neglected factor in heat alert systems and the lack of shade at the late-morning outdoor ceremony

To help improve HAPs, urban planner Kotharkar's team is working on a model plan that outlines best practices and could be adapted to local conditions. Among other things, she says, all cities should create a vulnerability map to help focus responses on the populations most at risk Kotharkar says. Such mapping doesn't need to be complex. A useful map can be created by looking at even a few key parameters.” For example. ,neighborhoods with a large elderly population or informal dwellings that cope poorly with heat could get special warnings or be bolstered with cooling centers. The Nagpur project has already created a risk and vulnerability map, which enabled Kotharkar to tell officials which neighborhoods to focus on in the event of a heat wave this summer

HAPs shouldn't just include short-term emergency responses, researchers say. but also recommend medium- to long-term measures that could make communities cooler. In Nagpur, for example, Kotharkar's team has been able to advise city officials about where to plant trees to provide shade. HAPs could also guide efforts to retrofit homes or modify building regulations. “Reducing deaths in an emergency is good target to have, but it's the lowest target,” says climate researchers Chandni Singh.
explanation: 细节题。根据题干关键词 Nagpur's plan 回文定位第一段：该计划要求医院夏季设“cold wards”（冷病房）救治中暑患者，并建议建筑商在极热天气让工人休息，两项措施都是为应对极端天气，故选 A。B“确保建筑质量”只是局部场景；C“监测紧急预警”、D“解决工作量过大”均属偷换。

passage:
Navigating beyond the organized pavements and parts of our urban spaces, desire paths are the unofficial footprints of a community, revealing the unspoken preferences, shared shortcuts and collective choices of humans. Often appearing as trodden dirt tracks through otherwise neat green spaces, these routes of collective disobedience cut corners, bisect lawns and cross hills, representing the natural capability of people (and animals) to go from point A to point B most effectively.

Urban planners interpret desire paths as more than just convenient shortcuts: they offer valuable insights into the dynamics between planning and behaviour. Ohio State University allowed its students to navigate the Oval, a lawn in the centre of campus, freely, then proceeded to pave the desire paths, creating a web of effective routes students had established

Yet, reluctance persists among other planners to integrate desire paths into formal plans, citing concerns about safety, environmental impact, or primarily aesthetics. A Reddit webpage devoted to the phenomenon, boasting nearly 50,000 members, showcases images of local desire paths adorned with signs instructing pedestrians to adhere to designated walkways, underscoring the rebellious nature inherent in these human-made tracks. This clash highlights an ongoing struggle between the organic, user-driven evolution of public spaces and the desire for a visually curated and controlled urban environment. The Wickauasgeck

Trail is an example of a historical desire path, created by Native Americans to cross the forests of Manhattan and move between settlements quickly. This trail. when Dutch colonists arrived, was, widened and made into one of the main trade roads across the island. known at the time as de Heere Straat, or Gentlemen's Street, Following the British assumption of control in New York, the street was renamed Broadway. Notably, Broadway stands out as one of the few areas in NYC that defies the grid-based system applied to the rest of the city, cutting a diagonal across parts of the city.

In online spaces, desire paths have sparked a fascination that can approach obsession, with the Reddit page serving as a hub. Contributors offer a wide array of stories, from little-known new shortcuts to long-established alternate routes.

Animal desire paths, such as ducks forging trails through frozen ponds or dogs carving direct routes in gardens, highlight the adaptability of these trails in both human and animal experiences As desire paths criss-cross through both physical and virtual landscapes, they stand as a proof of the collective insistence on forging unconventional routes and embracing the spirit of communal choice
explanation: 细节题。根据题干关键词 Paragraph 1 回文定位第一段：desire paths 体现人和动物“go from point A to point B most effectively”（从 A 到 B 最有效通行）的自然能力，shortcuts、most effectively 都指向“追求便利”，故选 C。A“探索山丘的好奇心”、B“保护绿地”、D“孤独中寻求慰藉”均与原文无关。

Urban planners interpret desire paths as more than just convenient shortcuts: they offer valuable insights into the dynamics between planning and behaviour. Ohio State University allowed its students to navigate the Oval, a lawn in the centre of campus, freely, then proceeded to pave the desire paths, creating a web of effective routes students had established

Yet, reluctance persists among other planners to integrate desire paths into formal plans, citing concerns about safety, environmental impact, or primarily aesthetics. A Reddit webpage devoted to the phenomenon, boasting nearly 50,000 members, showcases images of local desire paths adorned with signs instructing pedestrians to adhere to designated walkways, underscoring the rebellious nature inherent in these human-made tracks. This clash highlights an ongoing struggle between the organic, user-driven evolution of public spaces and the desire for a visually curated and controlled urban environment. The Wickauasgeck

Trail is an example of a historical desire path, created by Native Americans to cross the forests of Manhattan and move between settlements quickly. This trail. when Dutch colonists arrived, was, widened and made into one of the main trade roads across the island. known at the time as de Heere Straat, or Gentlemen's Street, Following the British assumption of control in New York, the street was renamed Broadway. Notably, Broadway stands out as one of the few areas in NYC that defies the grid-based system applied to the rest of the city, cutting a diagonal across parts of the city.

In online spaces, desire paths have sparked a fascination that can approach obsession, with the Reddit page serving as a hub. Contributors offer a wide array of stories, from little-known new shortcuts to long-established alternate routes.

Animal desire paths, such as ducks forging trails through frozen ponds or dogs carving direct routes in gardens, highlight the adaptability of these trails in both human and animal experiences As desire paths criss-cross through both physical and virtual landscapes, they stand as a proof of the collective insistence on forging unconventional routes and embracing the spirit of communal choice

How to Get Active Again After a Break

“Exercise is a miracle ‘drug,’ ” says Keri L. Denay, lead author of a recent American College of Sports Medicine advisory that encourages Americans to not overlook the benefits of activity during the pandemic.

Moving your body has been shown to reduce anxiety and depression, lower rates of many types of cancer and the risk of a heart attack, and improve overall immunity. It also helps build strength and stamina.

Getting back into exercise can be a challenge at the best of times, but with gyms and in-person exercise classes off-limits to many people these days because of COVID-19 concerns, it can be tricky to know where to start. And it’s important to get the right dose of activity. “Too much too soon either results in injury or burnout,” says Mary Yoke, a faculty member in the kinesiology department at Indiana University at Bloomington.

41. _______________________

Don’t try to go back to what you were doing before your break. If you were walking three miles a day, playing 18 holes of golf three times a week or lifting 10-pound dumbbells for three sets of 10 reps, reduce activity to a half-mile every other day, or nine holes of golf once a week with short walks on other days or use five-pound dumbbells for one set of 10 reps.

Increase time, distance and intensity gradually. “This isn’t something you can do overnight,” Denay says. But you’ll reap benefits such as less anxiety and improved sleep right away.

42. _______________________

If you’re breathing too hard to talk in complete sentences, back off. If you feel good, go a little longer or faster. Feeling wiped out after a session? Go easier next time. And stay alert to serious symptoms, such as chest pain or pressure, severe shortness of breath or dizziness, or faintness, and seek medical attention immediately.

43. _______________________

Consistency is the key to getting stronger and building endurance and stamina.

Ten minutes of activity per day is a good start, says Marcus Jackovitz, a physical therapist at the University of Miami Hospital. All the experts we spoke with highly recommend walking because it’s the easiest, most accessible form of exercise. Although it can be a workout on its own, if your goal is to get back to classes, tennis, cycling or any other activity, walking is also a great first step.

44. _______________________

Even if you can’t yet do a favorite activity, you can practice the moves. With or without a club or racket, swing like you’re hitting the ball. Paddle like you’re in a kayak or canoe. Mimic your favorite swimming strokes. The action will remind you of the joy the activity brought you and prime your muscles for when you can get out there again.

45. _______________________

Exercising with others “can keep you accountable and make it more fun, so you’re more likely to do it again,” Jackovitz says.

You can do activities such as golf and tennis or take a walk with others and still be socially distant. But when you can’t connect in person, consider using technology. Chat on the phone with a friend while you walk around your neighborhood. FaceTime or Zoom with a relative as you strength train or stretch at home.

You can also join a live stream or on-demand exercise class. SilverSneakers offers them for older adults, or try EverWalk for virtual challenges.

go slow(从低(标准)开始，慢慢来)是对原文信息的综合概括。所以本题选C。

Section III Translation
Although we try our best, sometimes our paintings rarely turn out as originally planned.
Changes in the light, the limitations of your painting materials, and the lack of experience and
technique mean that what you start out trying to achieve may not come to life the way that you
expected.
Although this can be frustrating and disappointing, it turns out that this can actually be good
for you. Unexpected results have two benefits: you pretty quickly learn to deal with
disappointment and realise that when one door closes, another opens. You also quickly learn to
adapt and come up with creative solutions to the problems the painting presents, and thinking
outside the box will become your second nature.
In fact, creative problem-solving skills are incredibly useful in daily life, with which you are
more likely to be able to find a solution when a problem arises.

How Colleges Weigh Applicants’ Extracurricular Activities

High school students eager to stand out in the college application process often participate in a litany of extracurricular activities hoping to bolster their chances of admission to a selective undergraduate institution.

However, college admissions experts say that the quality of a college hopeful’s extracurricular activities matters more than the number of activities he or she participates in.

Sue Rexford, the director of college guidance at the Charles E. Smith Jewish Day School, says it is not necessary for a student filling out the Common Application to list 10 activities in the application.

“No college will expect that a student has a huge laundry list of extracurriculars that they have been passionately involved in each for an extended period of time,” Rexford wrote in an email.

Experts say it is tougher to distinguish oneself in a school-affiliated extracurricular activity that is common among high school students than it is to stand out while doing an uncommon activity.

“The competition to stand out and make an impact is going to be much stiffer, and so if they’re going to do a popular activity, I’d say, be the best at it,” says Sara Harberson, a college admissions consultant.

High school students who have an impressive personal project they are working on independently often impress colleges, experts say.

“For example, a student with an interest in entrepreneurship could demonstrate skill and potential by starting a profitable small business,” Olivia Valdes, the founder of Zen Admissions consulting firm, wrote in an email.

Joseph Adegboyega-Edun, a Maryland high school guidance counselor, says unconventional extracurricular activities can help students impress college admissions offices, assuming they demonstrated serious commitment. “Again, since one of the big questions high school seniors must consider is ‘What makes you unique?,’ having an uncommon extracurricular activity vs. a conventional one is an advantage,” he wrote in an email.

Experts say demonstrating talent in at least one extracurricular activity can help in the college admissions process, especially at top-tier undergraduate institutions.

“Distinguishing yourself in one focused type of extracurricular activity can be a positive in the admissions process, especially for highly selective institutions, where having top grades and test scores is not enough,” Katie Kelley, admissions counselor at IvyWise admissions consultancy, wrote in an email. “Students need to have that quality or hook that will appeal to admissions officers and allow them to visualize how the student might come and enrich their campus community.”

Extracurricular activities related to the college major declared on a college application are beneficial, experts suggest. “If you already know your major, having an extracurricular that fits into that major can be a big plus,” says Mayghin Levine, the manager of educational opportunities with The Cabbage Patch Settlement House, a Louisville, Kentucky, nonprofit community center.

High school students who have had a strong positive influence on their community through an extracurricular activity may impress a college and win a scholarship, says Erica Gwyn, a former math and science magnet program assistant at a public high school who is now executive director of the Kaleidoscope Careers Academy in Atlanta, a nonprofit organization.

options.D: Human factors, as well as trees planted, should be emphasized in forest restoration
options.E: The supply of seeds is a tough problem that has to be dealt with

passage:
①In an effort to support restoration programmes, specialists are developing supplies of seeds and seedlings, maintaining gene banks and sequencing the genomes of indigenous trees and other crops. Their work deals with one of the problems that could block major restoration efforts in different parts of the world.

②“Where’s the planting material going to come from? That’s one big bottleneck,” says genetic-resources specialist Rami Jamnadass.

③Asia is arguably the region most neglected by global efforts to increase diversity in restoration and to study native species. Christopher Kettle, Bioversity International’s director for forest genetic resources and restoration in Rome, says that the need for infrastructure — things such as mechanisms for collecting and storing seeds, and nurseries to raise seedlings — might be most desperate here because many trees are ‘masting’ species, which don’t produce seeds every year. People need to be ready. “Otherwise, you miss the boat, you lose all the seed and you’ve got to wait another seven years,” says Kettle. “This is a really, really critical issue for restoration in Southeast Asia, because many of the most important timber species and tree species — the ones that will lock up the most carbon — they’re all masting species.”

④Climate change is a driving factor in the push to restore forests, but it also raises questions, such as where trees can thrive in the future. Climate change is also expected to alter relationships between trees, insects, diseases and other forest species. “Insects that today are a minor problem may become a major problem if they can produce three or four generations in a year,” says forest ecologist John Stanturf. This remains a significant knowledge gap. “We know enough to know that this is a concern, but we don’t know enough about how to respond to it yet. That’s a great area to be doing research.” So is soil, says Cindy Prescott, a forest ecologist at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver. “If you don’t look at the soil at the start, you can spend a lot of money and time putting in species that aren’t going to survive there.”

⑤With so much research left to do, leaders in the field have been doing some soul-searching, and acknowledging that restoration can be motivated by — and designed to meet — different needs. “When you talk about conservation or restoration, the first question has to be restoration by whom, for whom?” says Daniel Janzen, a biologist at the University of Pennsylvania.

⑥The question can have more than one answer. Much of the global funding for restoration is dedicated to developing it as a tool to mitigate climate change, notes restoration ecologist Pedro Brancalion. “But if you ask a farmer in Brazil if he or she is concerned about climate change, they would say, ‘No, I am concerned about water,’” he says. Their interests as stewards of the land need to be better integrated with those who have the money to support restoration.

⑦That has been the strongest lesson of all for forest ecologist Robin Chazdon. Restoration is about more than what gets planted in the ground, she says. “Yes, it’s about forests, but it’s really about people. They are the agents of restoration.”

That's one big bottleneck.」（种植材料从哪里来？这是个老大难问题。）planting material（种植材料）与 seed 同义复现，bottleneck（瓶颈、难题）说明种子供应亟待解决。E 项 The supply of seeds is a tough problem that has to be dealt with（种子供应是个必须解决的棘手问题）正是这句话的概括。故选 E。

⑦That has been the strongest lesson of all for forest ecologist Robin Chazdon. Restoration is about more than what gets planted in the ground, she says. “Yes, it’s about forests, but it’s really about people. They are the agents of restoration.”

stem: Pedro Brancalion

options.A: People must pay attention to the fact that some kinds of trees do not produce seeds annually
options.B: Soil is an important element to be taken into account in forest restoration
options.C: The purpose of restoration efforts may be different from the real needs of the people involved
options.D: Human factors, as well as trees planted, should be emphasized in forest restoration
options.E: The supply of seeds is a tough problem that has to be dealt with
options.F: When it comes to restoration, we have to stay with an awareness of whose interests to serve
options.G: Some creatures in the forest that multiply fast can become a great threat to forest restoration

passage:
①In an effort to support restoration programmes, specialists are developing supplies of seeds and seedlings, maintaining gene banks and sequencing the genomes of indigenous trees and other crops. Their work deals with one of the problems that could block major restoration efforts in different parts of the world.

②“Where’s the planting material going to come from? That’s one big bottleneck,” says genetic-resources specialist Rami Jamnadass.

③Asia is arguably the region most neglected by global efforts to increase diversity in restoration and to study native species. Christopher Kettle, Bioversity International’s director for forest genetic resources and restoration in Rome, says that the need for infrastructure — things such as mechanisms for collecting and storing seeds, and nurseries to raise seedlings — might be most desperate here because many trees are ‘masting’ species, which don’t produce seeds every year. People need to be ready. “Otherwise, you miss the boat, you lose all the seed and you’ve got to wait another seven years,” says Kettle. “This is a really, really critical issue for restoration in Southeast Asia, because many of the most important timber species and tree species — the ones that will lock up the most carbon — they’re all masting species.”

④Climate change is a driving factor in the push to restore forests, but it also raises questions, such as where trees can thrive in the future. Climate change is also expected to alter relationships between trees, insects, diseases and other forest species. “Insects that today are a minor problem may become a major problem if they can produce three or four generations in a year,” says forest ecologist John Stanturf. This remains a significant knowledge gap. “We know enough to know that this is a concern, but we don’t know enough about how to respond to it yet. That’s a great area to be doing research.” So is soil, says Cindy Prescott, a forest ecologist at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver. “If you don’t look at the soil at the start, you can spend a lot of money and time putting in species that aren’t going to survive there.”

⑤With so much research left to do, leaders in the field have been doing some soul-searching, and acknowledging that restoration can be motivated by — and designed to meet — different needs. “When you talk about conservation or restoration, the first question has to be restoration by whom, for whom?” says Daniel Janzen, a biologist at the University of Pennsylvania.

⑥The question can have more than one answer. Much of the global funding for restoration is dedicated to developing it as a tool to mitigate climate change, notes restoration ecologist Pedro Brancalion. “But if you ask a farmer in Brazil if he or she is concerned about climate change, they would say, ‘No, I am concerned about water,’” he says. Their interests as stewards of the land need to be better integrated with those who have the money to support restoration.

⑦That has been the strongest lesson of all for forest ecologist Robin Chazdon. Restoration is about more than what gets planted in the ground, she says. “Yes, it’s about forests, but it’s really about people. They are the agents of restoration.”
explanation: 阅读B（小标题匹配）。解题抓手是观点例证。⑥段 Pedro Brancalion 指出全球修复资金多服务于减缓气候变化，但「if you ask a farmer in Brazil... they would say, 'No, I am concerned about water'」（巴西农民关心的不是气候而是水）。可见修复目的与当地人的真实需求可能不一致。C 项 The purpose of restoration efforts may be different from the real needs of the people involved 准确概括了这一对比。故选 C。

stem: Directions： Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points) We tend to think that friends and family members are our biggest source of connection, laughter and warmth. While that may well be true, researchers have also recently found that interacting with strangers actually brings a boost in mood and feelings of belonging that we didn’t expect. In one series of studies, researchers instructed Chicago-area commuters using public transportation to strike up a conversation with someone near them. On average, participants who followed this instruction felt better than those who had been told to stand or sit in silence. The researchers also argued that when we shy away from casual interactions with strangers, it is often due to a misplaced anxiety that they might not want to talk to us. Much of the time, however, this belief is false. As it turns out, many people are actually perfectly willing to talk and may even be flattered to receive your attention.
explanation:
【参考译文】
我们往往认为，朋友和家人是我们获得人际联系、快乐与温暖的最大源泉。事实或许确实如此，但研究人员最近也发现，与陌生人交流实际上能提振情绪、增强归属感，这是我们始料未及的。
在其中一系列研究中，研究人员让芝加哥地区乘坐公共交通工具的通勤者主动与身旁的人攀谈。平均而言，照此执行的参与者比那些被要求安静站坐的人感觉更好。研究人员还指出，我们回避与陌生人的日常寒暄，往往是出于一种错位的焦虑——担心对方并不想搭理我们。然而多数情况下，这种想法是错误的。事实上，许多人非常乐意交谈，甚至会对你的关注感到受宠若惊。
【采分点】
1. connection 与 laughter、warmth 并列，指情感上的"联系、联结"，不宜译成"人脉"。
2. strike up a conversation 是固定搭配，意为"攀谈"，不能按字面直译。
3. that we didn't expect 是定语从句，修饰 boost，需拆分译出"这是我们始料未及的"。
4. misplaced anxiety 中 misplaced 意为"错位的、多余的"，暗含焦虑没有必要。
5. be flattered to receive your attention 被动转主动，译"因受到你的关注而受宠若惊"，语气更自然。

On average, participants who followed this instruction felt better than those who had been told to stand or sit in silence.

stem: Directions: Suppose you are organizing an online meeting. Write an email to Jack, an international student, to 1) invite him to participate, and 2) tell him the details. You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET. Do not use your own name. Use “Li Ming” instead. (10 points)
explanation:
【题目解读】你是线上会议的组织者，给留学生 Jack 写邮件：1) 邀请他参加；2) 告知具体细节。约100词，署名 Li Ming。时间、平台、每人时长等细节可合理自拟，但必须具体。
【段落结构】称呼 Dear Jack, → 开头一句话点明邀请目的 → 正文用 First/Second 覆盖两个要点 → 结尾盼复 → Yours sincerely, Li Ming。
【常见错误】只邀请不说细节，要点缺失；署真实姓名或漏署名；字数飙到130词以上；通篇命令式语气，缺乏客套；落款缺少 Yours sincerely。
【写作要领】两个要点都要落在具体信息上：邀请须点明活动主题，细节至少包含时间、形式、时长中的两三项；自拟细节要合理可信，如“7 p.m. October 24th”；语气用 I am writing to / I'd appreciate it if 等客套表达。
【卷面提示】词数控制在 90-110 之间；全文 3-4 段，每段 2-3 句；称呼顶格写，署名 Li Ming 后不加标点；书写工整，减少涂改。
【参考范文】
Dear Jack,
I hope everything is going on well with you. I am writing to sincerely invite you to join an online meeting themed "Foreign Students Tell Chinese Stories".
Several details are as follows. First, it will start at 7 p.m. on October 24th and last about two hours. Second, each participant is expected to present a Chinese story within 10-15 minutes, which will surely deepen your understanding of Chinese culture. Given your time in China, I am sure you will give a wonderful performance.
If interested, please reply at your earliest convenience. Looking forward to your reply!
Yours sincerely,
Li Ming

stem: Directions: Write an essay based on the chart below. In your writing, you should 1) interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. You should write about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
explanation:
【图表解读】某市居民体育锻炼方式调查（柱状图）：独自锻炼以 54.3% 居首，和朋友一起 47.7% 次之，与家人一起仅 23.9%，团体活动最少，只有 15.8%。描述时先总后分，用 ranks first / followed by / by contrast 等词衔接。可见独自锻炼最流行，集体形式遇冷。
【三段思路】首段描述图表：先总述调查对象，再用数据对比点明“独自锻炼占比最高、团体活动最低”；中段分析原因，建议从生活节奏、人口流动、文化观念三个角度展开；尾段总结展望，指出独自锻炼仍将是主流，也可适度呼吁人们参与集体运动。全文约 150 词，原因段每条原因只用一到两句话展开，避免堆砌；描述数据时精确到小数点后一位。
【亮点表达】account for / take up 占……比例；rank first 位居首位；be occupied with 忙于；be inclined to 倾向于；the alienation of interpersonal relationship 人际关系疏离；draw the conclusion that 得出结论。
【参考范文】
According to the bar chart, it demonstrates the differences in the manners of residents' physical exercise. Doing exercise alone ranks first, accounting for 54.30%, followed by doing sports with friends, taking up 47.7%. By contrast, exercising with family and joining group activities only account for 23.9% and 15.8% respectively.
Several factors are responsible for this phenomenon. First of all, occupied with heavy duties and chores, people hardly have extra time to make appointments with friends or join group activities. In addition, many people migrate to big cities for better opportunities, and the alienation of interpersonal relationships plus the fast pace make them more inclined to exercise alone.
Based on the discussion above, we can safely draw the conclusion that doing exercise alone will remain the leading choice among residents.

stem: Directions： Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points) Although we try our best, sometimes our paintings rarely turn out as originally planned. Changes in the light, the limitations of your painting materials and the lack of experience and technique mean that what you start out trying to achieve may not come to life the way that you expected. Although this can be frustrating and disappointing, it turns out that this can actually be good for you. Unexpected results have two benefits: you pretty quickly learn to deal with disappointment and realise that when one door closes, another opens. You also quickly learn to adapt and come up with creative solutions to the problems the painting presents and thinking outside the box will become your second nature. In fact, creative problem-solving skills are incredibly useful in daily life, with which you’re more likely to be able to find a solution when a problem arises.
explanation:
【参考译文】
尽管我们全力以赴，画作有时终究难以完全按照最初的构想呈现。光线的变化、绘画材料的局限，以及经验与技法的欠缺，都意味着一开始想要实现的效果，可能无法如预期般跃然纸上。
尽管这令人沮丧失望，但事实证明它对你其实大有裨益。意外的结果带来两点好处：你很快能学会应对失望，并领悟"当一扇门关闭时，另一扇门会为你打开"；你也能迅速学会适应，针对画作呈现的问题想出创造性的解法，于是"跳出框架思考"将成为你的第二天性。
事实上，创造性地解决问题的技能在日常生活中极为有用，有了它，问题出现时你更有可能找到解决方案。
【采分点】
1. turn out as planned：turn out 表"最终结果是"，整句译作"最终往往与计划不符"。
2. come to life 是固定搭配，本义"获得生命"，此处指画面"生动呈现、跃然纸上"。
3. when one door closes, another opens 是英语谚语，加引号译出更清晰。
4. the problems the painting presents 含省略 that 的定语从句，present 意为"呈现、带来"。
5. with which you're more likely to... 是"介词+which"从句，拆译为"有了它，你更有可能……"。

stem: Directions： Suppose you are planning a campus food festival. Write an email to the international students in your university, to 1) introduce the food festival, and 2) invite them to participate. You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET. Do not use your own name. Use “Li Ming” instead. (10 points)
explanation:
【题目解读】你是校园美食节的策划者，给全校国际学生写邮件：1) 介绍美食节；2) 邀请他们参加。约100词，署名 Li Ming。时间、地点、内容等细节可自拟，但要具体可信。
【段落结构】称呼 Dear International Students, → 开头点明事由 → 正文用 First/Second 介绍时间地点、内容亮点，并顺势发出邀请 → 结尾盼复 → Yours sincerely, Li Ming。
【常见错误】两个要点只写一个；介绍空洞，缺时间、地点、内容等细节；署真实姓名；语气像通知布告，生硬冷淡；落款缺少 Yours sincerely。
【写作要领】“介绍”要包含 What/When/Where 三要素，“邀请”须单独成句并表达期待，如 I sincerely invite you to join us；可再补一句参加的意义（品尝美食、结交朋友）增强说服力；结尾用 Looking forward to... 收束。
【卷面提示】词数控制在 90-110 之间；全文 3-4 段，每段 2-3 句；称呼顶格写，署名 Li Ming 后不加标点；书写工整，减少涂改。
【参考范文】
Dear International Students,
I am Li Ming, the organizer of the campus food festival. I am writing to introduce this event and sincerely invite you to join us.
The festival will be held this Saturday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. at the Students' Center. First, over 30 booths will offer delicacies from across China and around the world. Second, you may not only taste the food but also learn to cook a signature dish with our student chefs.
It is a great chance to enjoy delicious food and make new friends. Your participation will surely add color to the festival. Looking forward to seeing you there!
Yours sincerely,
Li Ming

stem: Directions: Write an essay based on the chart below. In your writing, you should 1) interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. You should write about 150 words on the on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
explanation:
【图表解读】2018-2020 我国快递业务量变化（柱状图，单位：十亿）：全国业务量从 51 增至 64 再到 83，农村从 12 增至 15 再到 30。三年间双双快速增长，农村基数虽小但增速更猛，2020 年已占全国三成以上。描述时先交代主题与单位，再分组对比，可用 rise from...to... 句型。
【三段思路】首段描述图表：先交代主题与单位，再分别概括全国与农村的增长，点明农村增速更快；中段分析原因，建议从电商发展、物流网络下沉、疫情推动线上消费三个角度展开；尾段总结展望，预计行业将保持增长，尤其农村市场潜力巨大。全文约 150 词，分析段每条原因展开一到两句即可。
【亮点表达】witness a sharp increase 见证激增；measured in billions 以十亿为单位；be attributed to 归因于；fuel the demand for 催生需求；the booming e-commerce 蓬勃发展的电商；the expansion of logistics networks 物流网络扩张。
【参考范文】
The bar chart illustrates the changes in China's express delivery volume from 2018 to 2020, measured in billions. The national volume rose steadily from 51 billion in 2018 to 83 billion in 2020. Meanwhile, the rural volume grew even faster, from 12 billion to 30 billion.
This dramatic increase can be attributed to several factors. First, the booming e-commerce and online shopping festivals have fueled demand for delivery services. Besides, the rapid expansion of logistics networks into rural areas has made delivery faster and cheaper. Finally, the pandemic pushed more consumers to shop online, further boosting the volume.
With continued investment in infrastructure, China's express delivery industry is expected to maintain strong growth, especially in rural markets.

stem: Directions: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points) In the late 18th century, William Wordsworth became famous for his poems about nature. And he was one of the founders of a movement called Romanticism, which celebrated the wonders of the natural world. Poetry is powerful. Its energy and rhythm can capture a reader, transport them to another world and make them see things differently. Through carefully selected words and phrases, poems can be dramatic, funny, beautiful, moving and inspiring. No one knows for sure when poetry began but it has been around for thousands of years, even before people could write. It was a way to tell stories and pass down history. It is closely related to song and even when written it is usually created to be performed out loud. Poems really come to life when they are recited. This can also help with understanding them too, because the rhythm and sounds of the words become clearer.
explanation:
【参考译文】
18 世纪晚期，威廉·华兹华斯因其描写自然的诗歌而声名鹊起。他还是浪漫主义运动的创始人之一，这场运动旨在赞美自然世界的奇观。
诗歌是强大的。它的力量与节奏能够俘获读者，将他们带入另一个世界，让他们以不同的眼光看待事物。借助精心挑选的词语和短语，诗歌可以戏剧、可以有趣、可以美丽、可以动人、可以鼓舞人心。
没有人确切知道诗歌起源于何时，但它已存在数千年，甚至在人们学会书写之前。它是讲述故事、传承历史的方式。诗歌与歌曲密切相关，即便是书面创作，通常也是为了高声吟诵而作。诗歌在被朗诵时才真正鲜活起来。这也有助于理解诗歌，因为词语的节奏与音韵变得更加清晰。
【采分点】
1. became famous for：表原因，译为"因……而闻名"，语序调整为"以其自然诗作声名鹊起"。
2. celebrated the wonders：celebrate 此处意为"赞颂、颂扬"，而非"庆祝"。
3. capture a reader：capture 由"捕获"引申为"吸引、打动"，译"俘获读者"最贴切。
4. pass down history：固定搭配，"传承历史"，down 含代际相传之意。
5. come to life：意为"鲜活起来"，主语转为朗诵行为，译"被朗诵时才真正鲜活"。

scoring.ref: 18 世纪晚期，威廉·华兹华斯因其描写自然的诗歌而声名鹊起。他还是浪漫主义运动的创始人之一，这场运动旨在赞美自然世界的奇观。诗歌是强大的。它的力量与节奏能够俘获读者，将他们带入另一个世界，让他们以不同的眼光看待事物。借助精心挑选的词语和短语，诗歌可以戏剧、可以有趣、可以美丽、可以动人、可以鼓舞人心。没有人确切知道诗歌起源于何时，但它已存在数千年，甚至在人们学会书写之前。它是讲述故事、传承历史的方式。诗歌与歌曲密切相关，即便是书面创作，通常也是为了高声吟诵而作。诗歌在被朗诵时才真正鲜活起来。这也有助于理解诗歌，因为词语的节奏与音韵变得更加清晰。

groups.en: In the late 18th century, William Wordsworth became famous for his poems about nature.
And he was one of the founders of a movement called Romanticism, which celebrated the wonders of the natural world.
Poetry is powerful.
Its energy and rhythm can capture a reader, transport them to another world and make them see things differently.
Through carefully selected words and phrases, poems can be dramatic, funny, beautiful, moving and inspiring.
No one knows for sure when poetry began but it has been around for thousands of years, even before people could write.
It was a way to tell stories and pass down history.
It is closely related to song and even when written it is usually created to be performed out loud.
Poems really come to life when they are recited.
This can also help with understanding them too, because the rhythm and sounds of the words become clearer.

stem: Directions: An art exhibition and a robot show are to be held on Sunday, and your friend David asks you which one he should go to. Write him an email to 1) make a suggestion, and 2) give your reason(s). You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET. Do not use your own name, use “Li Ming” instead.(10 points)
explanation:
【题目解读】朋友 David 周日纠结该去艺术展还是机器人展，写邮件给他：1) 给出明确建议；2) 说明理由。约100词，署名 Li Ming。两个活动都要提及，但立场必须鲜明，不能模棱两可。
【段落结构】称呼 Dear David, → 开头回应他的求助并亮明建议 → 正文用 First/Besides 给出两条理由 → 结尾提醒与祝福 → Best regards, Li Ming。
【常见错误】只给建议不解释，或反之；两个都推荐、没有明确倾向；理由空洞；结尾忘署名；通篇祈使句，语气生硬。
【写作要领】建议要直说，如 I recommend the robot show；理由可从“与专业相关”“时间成本（展期长短）”“结伴同行”等角度任选其二，做到具体、有说服力；结尾可顺带提醒报名或集合安排。
【卷面提示】词数控制在 90-110 之间；全文 3-4 段，每段 2-3 句；称呼顶格写，署名 Li Ming 后不加标点；书写工整，减少涂改。
【参考范文】
Dear David,
I am glad to hear from you. As for the art exhibition and the robot show this Sunday, I recommend the robot show.
First and foremost, the robot show is more practical and instructive, which is closely related to your major and future career. Besides, the art exhibition will last for many days, so you can visit it another day, while the robot show is a rare chance. On that day, I will also be there, so we could go together.
Remember to register on its official website in advance. I sincerely hope you will enjoy yourself. See you soon!
Best regards,
Li Ming

stem: Directions: Write an essay based on the chart below. In your essay, you should 1) describe the picture briefly, interpret the implied meaning, 2) give your comments. You should write about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
explanation:
【图表解读】2012-2021 年我国居民健康素养水平（折线图）：十年间由 8.80% 稳步攀升至 25.40%。其中 2013-2016 年增长平缓（9%-12%），2017 年起明显提速，从 11.58% 一路升至 25.40%。折线图常用 rise steadily / grow slowly / increase dramatically 等趋势词，注意平缓期与提速期的对比，纵轴单位是百分比。
【三段思路】首段描述图表：先点明主题是健康素养水平变化，再概括总体趋势“持续上升”，可补充前期平缓、后期提速的阶段特征；中段分析原因，建议从公众健康意识、新媒体科普、政府政策与免费体检两个层面展开；尾段总结展望，指出提升是意识与政策合力的结果，未来仍有上升空间。全文约 150 词，每条原因展开一两句。
【亮点表达】witness a steady increase 见证稳步增长；be bound up with 与……密切相关；have access to 获得；play an important role 发挥重要作用；keep rising 持续上升；draw a conclusion 得出结论。
【参考范文】
Judging from the line graph, we can clearly see that China's residents' health literacy level rose steadily from 8.80% in 2012 to 25.40% in 2021, though it grew slowly between 2013 and 2016.
This remarkable improvement is bound up with several factors. To begin with, people's awareness of health has been increasing. With apps like Douyin and Weibo, abundant health knowledge has been widely spread, helping people adopt healthier lifestyles. In addition, the government's health policies and programs, such as free physical examinations, have also played an important role.
Based on the factors above, we can safely conclude that this improvement results from both people's growing awareness and government support, and the level will keep rising in the future.

stem: Directions: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points) With the smell of coffee and fresh bread floating in the air, stalls bursting with colourful vegetables and tempting cheeses, and the buzz of friendly chats, farmers’ markets are a feast for the senses. They also provide an opportunity to talk to the people responsible for growing or raising your food, support your local economy and pick up fresh seasonal produce — all at the same time. Farmers’ markets are usually weekly or monthly events, most often with outdoor stalls, which allow farmers or producers to sell their food directly to customers. The size or regularity of markets can vary from season to season, depending on the area’s agricultural calendar, and you’re likely to find different produce on sale at different times of the year. By cutting out the middleman, the farmers secure more profit for their produce. Shoppers also benefit from seeing exactly where — and to who — their money is going.
explanation:
【参考译文】
空气中飘荡着咖啡与新鲜面包的香气，摊位上摆满了色彩缤纷的蔬菜和诱人的奶酪，还有人们友好闲聊的嗡嗡声——农贸市场堪称一场感官盛宴。它们还让你有机会与负责种植、饲养你食材的人直接交谈，支持本地经济，同时还能买到新鲜的时令农产品。
农贸市场通常是每周或每月举办一次的活动，大多设有户外摊位，让农户或生产者直接向顾客销售食品。市场规模和举办频率因季节而异，取决于当地农事安排，一年中不同时节你很可能看到不同的农产品在售。由于省去中间商，农户能从产品中获得更多利润，顾客也能确切知道自己的钱流向了哪里、给了谁。
【采分点】
1. a feast for the senses 是固定搭配，"感官盛宴"；前面三个并列名词短语需拆解并重组句式。
2. the people responsible for growing or raising your food 是后置定语，译为"负责种植、饲养你食材的人"，定语提前。
3. allow farmers or producers to sell... 是 allow sb. to do 结构，与 which 定语从句一起拆分翻译。
4. agricultural calendar 意为"农业日历、农事安排"，切不可误作"农历节令"。
5. cutting out the middleman 中 cut out 意为"省去、去掉"；文末 to who 应为 to whom，介词+关系代词，译"给了谁"。

They also provide an opportunity to talk to the people responsible for growing or raising your food, support your local economy and pick up fresh seasonal produce — all at the same time.
Farmers’ markets are usually weekly or monthly events, most often with outdoor stalls, which allow farmers or producers to sell their food directly to customers.
The size or regularity of markets can vary from season to season, depending on the area’s agricultural calendar, and you’re likely to find different produce on sale at different times of the year.
By cutting out the middleman, the farmers secure more profit for their produce.
Shoppers also benefit from seeing exactly where — and to who — their money is going.

stem: Directions: Suppose you and Jack are going to do a survey on the protection of old houses in an ancient town. Write him an email to 1) put forward your plan, and 2) ask for his opinion. Write your answer in about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET. Do not use your own name in your email; use “Li Ming” instead. (10 points)
explanation:
【题目解读】你和 Jack 将赴某古镇开展老宅保护调研，写邮件给他：1) 提出你的计划；2) 征求他的意见。约100词，署名 Li Ming。计划中的时间、分工等细节可自拟，但要有条理、可执行。
【段落结构】称呼 Dear Jack, → 开头说明调研背景 → 正文用 First/Second/Finally 分列计划（时间安排、调研内容、总结讨论）→ 结尾征求意见 → Yours sincerely, Li Ming。
【常见错误】计划写成流水账，没有层次；忘记"征求意见"这一必备要点；语气生硬像下命令；字数过长或过短；细节自相矛盾，如时间冲突。
【写作要领】计划按时间顺序分两到三点陈述最清晰，如集合时间、测量拍摄、入户访谈、汇总讨论；征求意见要用征询口吻，如 Do you think the schedule is reasonable / I would like to hear your opinion。
【卷面提示】词数控制在 90-110 之间；全文 3-4 段，每段 2-3 句；称呼顶格写，署名 Li Ming 后不加标点；书写工整，减少涂改。
【参考范文】
Dear Jack,
I am glad that we will conduct a survey on the protection of old houses in the ancient town this weekend. Here is my plan, and I would like to hear your opinion.
First, we will set out at 8 a.m. on Saturday, measuring and photographing several well-preserved houses. Second, we plan to interview local residents about the history and current problems of these buildings. Finally, we will summarize our findings and discuss possible protection measures in the afternoon.
Do you think the schedule is reasonable? If you have any suggestions, please let me know. Looking forward to your early reply.
Yours sincerely,
Li Ming

stem: Directions: Write an essay based on the chart below. In your writing, you should 1) describe and interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. Write your answer in about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
explanation:
【图表解读】某高校实践活动课学生主要收获调查（条形图）：学习了相关知识高达 91.3%，提升了劳动能力 84.8%，感觉到了心情舒畅 54.5%，增强了合作能力仅 32.6%。条形图可按从高到低顺序描述，用 as is depicted / by contrast 衔接。可见课程在知识技能层面收获显著，而在情感体验与合作能力上相对不足。
【三段思路】首段描述图表：先交代调查对象，再按高低顺序罗列数据，指出知识、能力类收获占比高，情感与合作类偏低；中段分析原因，建议从课程偏重技能传授、缺乏协作任务设计、引导不足等角度展开；尾段提出建议并展望，呼吁丰富活动形式、加强团队协作与指导。全文约 150 词，措施段用 Only in this way can... 倒装收尾更有力度。
【亮点表达】account for / take up 占比；as is depicted 如图所示；be attributed to 归因于；cooperative ability 合作能力；all-round development 全面发展；be conducive to 有助于。
【参考范文】
The bar chart shows a survey on the main gains of students from practical activity courses in a university. As is depicted, 91.3% of the students have learned relevant knowledge, and 84.8% have improved their working ability. By contrast, only 54.5% feel delighted and 32.6% have enhanced their cooperative ability.
The data reveal that practical courses mainly focus on knowledge and skills, while their roles in emotional satisfaction and teamwork are relatively limited, which may be attributed to the lack of well-designed group tasks and sufficient guidance.
To address this, universities should enrich the forms of practical activities, encourage more teamwork, and provide timely guidance. Only in this way can these courses be conducive to students' all-round development.

stem: Directions: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points) The influence of wearables on psychology refers to how the clothes we wear affect our thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. Clothing is not just about covering our bodies; it plays a significant role in shaping our self-perception and interactions with others. One aspect of this influence is self-expression. The clothes we choose can reflect our personality, mood, and identity. Whether we opt for bold, colorful outfits or prefer more understated styles, our dress choices convey messages about who we are and how we want to be perceived. Additionally, clothing can impact our confidence levels. When we wear clothes that make us feel comfortable and confident, it can positively affect our self-esteem and overall mood. Moreover, cultural and societal influences play a significant role in shaping our dress choices. Different cultures have their norms and expectations regarding dress, which can influence the types of clothing people wear and the meanings attributed to them.
explanation:
【参考译文】
可穿戴服饰对心理的影响，指的是我们所穿着的衣物如何影响我们的思维、情感和行为。服装不仅仅是为了遮体，它在塑造自我认知以及与他人的互动中发挥着重要作用。
这种影响的一个方面是自我表达。我们所选择的衣物可以反映出我们的个性、情绪和身份认同。无论我们选择大胆鲜艳的着装，还是偏爱更为低调的风格，我们的穿衣选择都在传递关于我们是谁以及我们希望如何被看待的信息。此外，着装能够影响我们的自信心。研究表明，穿着我们感觉良好或认为有吸引力的衣服，可以对我们的自尊和整体情绪产生积极影响。
再者，文化和社会的影响在塑造我们的穿衣选择方面起着重要作用。不同的文化对于着装有着各自的规范和期望，这会影响人们穿着的服装类型及其被赋予的意义。
【采分点讲解】
1. wearables 译「可穿戴服饰」，与 clothes 对应；influence on... 译「对……的影响」。
2. plays a significant role in shaping our self-perception and interactions with others 译「在塑造自我认知以及与他人的互动中发挥着重要作用」；play a significant role in doing sth.，中文把「发挥着重要作用」后置收尾，属语序调整。
3. Whether we opt for bold, colorful outfits or prefer more understated styles 译「无论我们选择大胆鲜艳的着装，还是偏爱更为低调的风格」；whether...or... 译「无论……还是……」；opt for 意为选择；understated 意为低调。
4. positively affect our self-esteem and overall mood 译「对我们的自尊和整体情绪产生积极影响」；self-esteem 译「自尊」，overall mood 译「整体情绪」，positively 转作「积极的」。
5. the meanings attributed to them 译「被赋予的意义」；attributed to 为被动结构，译「被赋予」，them 指 clothing，需点明「服装」。

scoring.ref: 可穿戴服饰对心理的影响，指的是我们所穿着的衣物如何影响我们的思维、情感和行为。服装不仅仅是为了遮体，它在塑造自我认知以及与他人的互动中发挥着重要作用。这种影响的一个方面是自我表达。我们所选择的衣物可以反映出我们的个性、情绪和身份认同。无论我们选择大胆鲜艳的着装，还是偏爱更为低调的风格，我们的穿衣选择都在传递关于我们是谁以及我们希望如何被看待的信息。此外，着装能够影响我们的自信心。当我们穿着让自己感觉舒适和自信的衣服时，它能够对我们的自尊和整体情绪产生积极影响。再者，文化和社会的影响在塑造我们的穿衣选择方面起着重要作用。不同的文化对于着装有着各自的规范和期望，这会影响人们穿着的服装类型及其被赋予的意义。

groups.en: The influence of wearables on psychology refers to how the clothes we wear affect our thoughts, feelings, and behaviors.
Clothing is not just about covering our bodies; it plays a significant role in shaping our self-perception and interactions with others.
One aspect of this influence is self-expression.
The clothes we choose can reflect our personality, mood, and identity.
Whether we opt for bold, colorful outfits or prefer more understated styles, our dress choices convey messages about who we are and how we want to be perceived.
Additionally, clothing can impact our confidence levels.
When we wear clothes that make us feel comfortable and confident, it can positively affect our self-esteem and overall mood.
Moreover, cultural and societal influences play a significant role in shaping our dress choices.
Different cultures have their norms and expectations regarding dress, which can influence the types of clothing people wear and the meanings attributed to them.

stem: Directions： Suppose your friend Jack has shared with you a video of his family’s travel in China. Write an email to tell him (1) how you feel about the video, and (2) your wish to learn more about their travel. Write you answer in about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET. Do not use your own name in your email; Use “Li Ming” instead.(10 points)
explanation:
题目要求解读：本文是书信体应用文（10 分）。角色定位：你（Li Ming）给朋友 Jack 回信；Jack 刚分享了家人来中国旅行的视频。必须覆盖两个要点：①谈谈你对这个视频的感受；②表达想进一步了解他们旅行的愿望。字数约 100 词，署名统一用 Li Ming，语气应亲切自然。
建议段落结构：第一段寒暄并总体评价视频（景色震撼、文化气息真实、引人入胜）；第二段谈印象最深的片段，顺势引出想听更多旅行故事；第三段表达期待并署名。
常见错误提醒：漏写「想了解更多」这一必备要点；署名用了真实姓名；把信件写成公文腔，缺乏朋友间的亲切感；严重超过 100 词。
高分提示：感受要具体，可点名视频里的景物或文化细节；愿望要顺势而发，与上文衔接自然；全文控制在 90-110 词。
参考范文：
Dear Jack,
I just finished watching your family's travel video in China, and I was absolutely captivated by it! The landscapes you filmed were breathtaking, and the way you captured the local culture felt so genuine and immersive. It truly felt like I was travelling alongside you.
The segment about the traditional village particularly caught my interest. The architecture and daily life there looked fascinating. I'd love to hear more about your experiences there and any other interesting stories from your trip that didn't make it into the video.
Looking forward to catching up soon and hearing all about your adventures in more detail.
Yours sincerely,
Li Ming

stem: Directions: Write an essay based on the chart below. In your essay, you should 1) describe and interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. You answer in about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points) 某项关于儿童户外活动看法的调查
explanation:
图表内容解读：这是一张关于儿童户外活动看法的调查柱状图，共统计四个项目——「满足好奇心」占 54.6%，「促进观察力」占 54.5%，两者几乎持平且遥遥领先；「强身健体」占 37.2%，「增强亲子互动」占 33.2%，均在三成多。数据说明家长最看重户外活动对孩子认知与探索能力的培养，其次才是身体锻炼和亲子陪伴；写作文时需把四个数据按高低顺序全部点到。
三段式写作思路：①描述图表——按从高到低的顺序呈现数据，用对比突出两项认知类益处以约 54.5% 的比例明显领先，其余两项在三成上下；②分析原因——数字时代家长更重视让孩子走出屏幕、在自然探索中学习，亲子互动也反映了对情感陪伴的需求；③总结展望——户外活动是促进儿童全面成长的重要途径，应切实保障孩子亲近自然的机会。
参考范文：
The chart presents the findings of a survey on the perceived benefits of children's outdoor activities. According to the data, 「satisfying curiosity」 and 「improving observation skills」 are considered the most significant advantages, recognized by 54.6% and 54.5% of respondents respectively. Following closely, 「enhancing physical fitness」 is acknowledged by 37.2% of participants, while 「strengthening parent-child interaction」 is valued by 33.2%.
This data reveals a profound shift in parental focus, prioritizing cognitive and exploratory development over purely physical outcomes. The high value placed on curiosity and observation suggests an awareness that outdoor environments serve as vital, unstructured classrooms where children learn through discovery and sensory engagement. Meanwhile, the recognition of parent-child interaction highlights an understanding of the relational and emotional benefits derived from shared outdoor experiences. In an age dominated by digital screens, these findings underscore a collective yearning for reconnection with the natural world as a foundation for holistic growth.
In conclusion, the survey underscores that outdoor activities are not merely recreational but essential for nurturing inquisitive, observant, and well-rounded individuals. Parents and educators should therefore actively create and protect opportunities for children to explore, play, and connect outdoors.

stem: Directions: Translate the following text from English into Chinese, Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET (15 points) You know the moment-the conversation slows and then there's a pause. It's awkward, and so awkward that some people will panic and say anything. Do we all find such silences so stressful?
explanation:
【参考译文】你一定知道这样的时刻——谈话渐渐放缓，随后便是一段沉默。这很尴尬，尴尬到有些人会惊慌失措，干脆随便说点什么。是不是所有人都觉得这种沉默如此令人焦虑？
研究人员分析了对话中超过 2 秒的停顿的出现频率及其影响，其中还包括对以往研究的综述。这些研究表明，人们对尴尬沉默的恐惧可能极其强烈，以至于会避免与陌生人交谈，尽管与陌生人交谈很可能是一次愉快的体验。
在仅有短暂停顿的对话中，人们会感觉与交谈对象更为亲近；但这种亲近感一旦遇到长时间停顿便会明显下降。陌生人之间出现长时间停顿后，话题很可能发生转换。
但朋友之间的对话似乎恰恰相反：长时间的停顿反而让彼此更亲近。在朋友之间，较长的停顿似乎为反思与表达提供了自然的间隙。
采分点讲解：① “the conversation slows” 中 slow 结合语境译“渐渐放缓、冷场”，勿直译“变慢”；② “so awkward that... panic and say anything” 用 so...that... 句型，译“如此尴尬以至于惊慌失措、随便说点什么”，say anything 指随便说点什么来打破沉默；③ “gaps greater than 2 seconds” 中 gaps 指对话中的“停顿、间隙”，勿误作“差距”；④ “including an overview of previous studies which indicate that...” 是长句，宜把 which 从句拆译：“其中还包括对以往研究的综述。这些研究表明……”；⑤ “Long gaps there saw increased connection” 中 saw 表“伴随、产生”，there 指 between friends，应意译为“长时间的停顿反而让彼此更亲近”。

stem: Directions: Suppose you are planning a short play based on a classic Chinese novel. Write your friend John an e-mail to 1)introduce the play, and 2) invite him to take part in it. You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEFT Do not use your own name.Use “Li Ming” instead.(10 points)
explanation:
题目要求解读：你是 Li Ming，给朋友 John 写一封电子邮件，必须覆盖两个要点：1) introduce the play——介绍改编自经典中国小说的短剧（剧名、出处、剧情亮点）；2) invite him to take part in it——邀请他参演。全文约 100 词，落款必须署名 Li Ming，语气是对朋友的友好非正式口吻。
建议段落结构：第一段说明来意并简介短剧；第二段发出邀请——请他出演某角色或参与演出，附上时间地点与理由；第三段表达期待、友好收尾。
常见错误提醒：① 漏要点——只介绍剧情忘了邀请，或只邀请没介绍剧情，两个要点必须都覆盖；② 署名错误——必须写 Li Ming，写真实姓名或不署名都会扣分；③ 字数失衡——超过 150 词或不足 70 词都会影响得分；④ 格式缺失——电子邮件需有称呼（Dear John）与落款（Yours 等）。
参考范文：
Dear John,
How is everything going? I'm planning a short play based on the classic Chinese novel Journey to the West, and I'd like to invite you to join us.
The play retells how the Monkey King and his companions overcome difficulties on their journey westward. We will stage it in the university hall next month, with colorful costumes and humorous dialogue. Since you are outgoing and good at acting, you would be perfect for the role of the Monkey King.
I do hope you can take part in it. Looking forward to your reply!
Yours,
Li Ming

explanation:
图表解读：这是一幅题为“某社区老年人主要休闲活动调查”的柱状图，显示五类活动的人数百分比：看电视 90.8%，散步 68.3%，养花 34.7%，阅读 31.8%，下棋 18.4%。看电视占绝对主导，散步次之，其余三项均不足 40%，可见社区老年人的休闲方式以居家静态活动为主，较为单一。
写作思路（三段式）：第一段描述图表——点明调查主题，按由高到低的顺序罗列数据，并概括“看电视为主、散步为辅”的总体特征；第二段分析原因/影响——退休后闲暇增多但社交圈缩小，看电视门槛最低、无需出门和找伙伴；公园步道等设施完善使散步成为最普及的户外活动；阅读、下棋受场地与伙伴限制，占比偏低；静态休闲过多不利于身心健康；第三段总结展望——社区应增设活动场所、组织集体项目，引导更健康、更多元的休闲方式。
参考范文：
The chart presents a survey on the main leisure activities of elderly people in a certain community. As is shown, watching TV ranks first, accounting for 90.8% of the respondents. It is followed by taking walks (68.3%), while gardening, reading and playing chess account for 34.7%, 31.8% and 18.4% respectively.
Several factors may explain this phenomenon. To begin with, most retired elderly people have plenty of free time but a shrinking social circle, and watching TV, which requires neither going out nor finding partners, naturally becomes their first choice. In addition, improved facilities such as parks and footpaths make walking the most accessible outdoor activity. By contrast, reading and chess demand specific venues or companions, so their percentages are much lower.
In conclusion, the leisure life of the elderly remains relatively monotonous. Communities should provide more activity centers and organize group events, encouraging seniors to take up healthier and more diversified pastimes.

stem: What problem are U.S. national parks faced with?
passage:
It􀆳s easy to dismiss as absurd the federal government􀆳s ideas for plugging the chronic funding gap of our national parks. Can anyone really think it􀆳s a good idea to allow Amazon deliveries to your tent in Yosemite or food trucks to line up under the redwood trees at Sequoia National Park?

But the government is right about one thing: U.S. national parks are in crisis. Collectively, they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion. Roads, trails, rest rooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling.

But privatizing and commercializing the campgrounds would not be a cure-all. Campgrounds are a tiny portion of the overall infrastructure backlog, and businesses in the parks hand over, on average, only about 5% of their revenues to the National Park Service. Moreover, increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat that overwhelms daily life.

The real problem is that the parks have been chronically starved of funding. An economic survey of 700 U.S. taxpayers found that people would be willing to pay a significant amount of money to make sure the parks and their programs are kept intact. Some 81% of respondents said they would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts to the national parks.

The national parks provide great value to U.S. residents both as places to escape and as symbols of nature. On top of this, they produce value from their extensive educational programs, their positive impact on the climate through carbon sequestration, their contribution to our cultural and artistic life, and of course through tourism. The parks also help keep America􀆳s past alive, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to protect historical sites and to bring the stories of these places to life.

The parks do all this on a shoestring. Congress allocates only $3 billion a year to the national park system—an amount that has been flat since 2001 (in inflation-adjusted dollars) with the exception of a onetime boost in 2009. Meanwhile, the number of annual visitors has increased by more than 50% since 1980, and now stands at 330 million visitors per year.

stem: Sparrow􀆳s study shows that with the Internet, the human brain will
passage:
The Internet may be changing merely what we remember, not our capacity to do so, suggests Columbia University psychology professor Betsy Sparrow. In 2011, Sparrow led a study in which participants were asked to record 40 factoids in a computer (“an ostrich􀆳s eye is bigger than its brain,” for example). Half of the participants were told the information would be erased, while the other half were told it would be saved. Guess what? The latter group made no effort to recall the information when quizzed on it later, because they knew they could find it on their computers. In the same study, a group was asked to remember both the information and the folders it was stored in. They didn􀆳t remember the information, but they remembered how to find the folders. In other words, human memory is not deteriorating but “adapting to new communications technology,” Sparrow says.

In a very practical way, the Internet is becoming an external hard drive for our memories, a process known as “cognitive offloading.” Traditionally, this role was fulfilled by data banks, libraries, and other humans. Your father may never remember birthdays because your mother does, for instance. Some worry that this is having a destructive effect on society, but Sparrow sees an upside. Perhaps, she suggests, the trend will change our approach to learning from a focus on individual facts and memorization to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking—something that is not available on the Internet. “I personally have never seen all that much intellectual value in memorizing things.” Sparrow says, adding that we haven􀆳t lost our ability to do it.

Still other experts say it􀆳s too soon to understand how the Internet affects our brains. There is no experimental evidence showing that it interferes with our ability to focus, for instance, wrote psychologists Christopher Chabris and Daniel J. Simons. And surfing the web exercised the brain more than reading did among computer-savvy older adults in a 2008 study involving 24 participants at the Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior at the University of California, Los Angeles.

“There may be costs associated with our increased reliance on the Internet, but I􀆳d have to imagine that overall the benefits are going to outweigh those costs,” observes psychology professor Benjamin Storm. “It seems pretty clear that memory is changing, but is it changing for the better? At this point, we don􀆳t know.”
explanation: 细节题。根据题文同序原则以及题干关键词“Sparrow's study, human brain”回文定位到第三段。选项的共性是都是动词开头，也就是需要找出人类大脑将会做什么事情。该段倒数第二、三句提到：“In the same study, a group was asked to remember both the information and the folders it was stored in. They didn't remember the information, but they remembered how to find the folders.”（在同一项研究中，一组人被要求记住信息和存储信息的文件夹。他们不记得信息，但记住了如何找到文件夹。）可见现在人们头脑中记住的事物发生了改变——从记住信息本身转向记住获取信息的途径。C 项 switch its focus of memory（转变记忆的重心）与原文形成呼应，故选 C。其余选项：A 项 analyze information in detail（详细分析信息）、B 项 collect information efficiently（高效收集信息）、D 项 extend its memory duration（延长记忆时长）均与实验结果不符。
